state.initial_idea: Recreate the dynamic workflow set up shown in the article https://bun.com/blog/bun-in-rust (Bun's Zig-to-Rust rewrite using Claude Code dynamic workflows: implementer + 2 adversarial diff-only reviewers + fixer, prep docs, compiler-error queue, test loops, parallel worktrees)

rounds.question: When this is built and running, what is it actually doing? (deliverable shape)
rounds.answer: Reusable toolkit + demo: build the workflow system as a reusable toolkit in this repo, validated end-to-end on a small sample codebase

rounds.question: Dex ships SDKs for Go, Java, Python, Rust, and TypeScript. Which SDK do we build on?
How should the implementer / adversarial reviewers / fixer subagents actually invoke the LLM inside dex steps?
rounds.answer: Hybrid: in-process API calls for adversarial reviewers and analysis (diff-in, verdict-out) plus CLI agents for implementer/fixer work

rounds.question: What if adversarial reviewers catch nothing and you can't tell a working setup from a rubber-stamp — what evidence would make you say 'yes, that's it'?
rounds.answer: Metrics report + Durability proof (NOT seeded-bug demo, NOT green-tests-only)

rounds.question: What operation does the demo actually perform (port pairing / modernization / pluggable)?
rounds.answer: CORRECTED in Round 6: Port PHP to TypeScript — small sample PHP module ported using the full pipeline (spec map, per-symbol analysis, port loop, typecheck queue); verification on TS side, PHP source read-only

rounds.question: What's the simplest version of the concurrency harness + dex infrastructure that still delivers metrics report + durability proof? (also: Round 5 answer corrected to PHP->TypeScript)
rounds.answer: Minimal v1: one local dex server (docker compose or binary), 2 git worktrees, ~4-6 agents, single port workflow, git-safety rules enforced, low concurrency cap

rounds.question: How big is the sample PHP project the demo ports (generated in-repo as fixture)?
rounds.answer: Small: ~6-10 PHP files, ~400-700 LOC, plus a handful of test files

rounds.question: Which agent stack powers the roles (recalling hybrid: reviewers in-process, implementer/fixer CLI)?
rounds.answer: Custom harness in opencode, similar to oh-my-openagent: TypeScript opencode plugin (agents + skills as TS modules, oh-my-openagent architecture), driven programmatically by dex flows via opencode server/SDK

rounds.question: How should the two adversarial reviewers execute (raw API vs opencode sessions)?
rounds.answer: All roles in opencode: reviewers are opencode sessions with a read-only adversarial-reviewer agent (diff-in, structured verdict-out, no write tools)

rounds.question: Which acceptance items are hard requirements for v1 (durability kill+resume, metrics report, demo-completes-green, reusable docs)?
rounds.answer: Durability: kill + resume (Required), Metrics report (Required) — demo-completes-green and reusable docs NOT required
